final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a more caveated reading of the same record. That reframing is more disciplined than the original clean-certification posture, but it still does not establish the missing compliance facts. On the available evidence summary, the enterprise refund workflow remains below target, is connected to customer-renewal commitments, legal review is still open, and no approved risk-acceptance or completed disclosure record is identified. Under the stated decision criteria, operational readiness evidence and public monitoring guidance do not by themselves satisfy an internal materiality-disclosure predicate. The Actor's caveated position may be arguable as a governance recommendation, but it is not enough to upgrade the audit outcome to compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is itself an unresolved compliance condition rather than a residual monitoring item.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added after the initial report; the Actor explicitly offered none.
The core compliance predicate remains unresolved: no admissible record shows the segment gap was resolved, disclosed pre-launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, not satisfaction of the policy's materiality/disclosure requirement.
The policy text cuts against relying on 'non-core' or low-volume framing when legal review is pending and customer-commitment relevance is in the record.
The Actor's narrowed position is a reframing of the same evidence into a caveated certification argument, not proof that the required policy conditions were met.
